question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the maximum value of the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-yz$ on the intersection of the surfaces $y+{z}^{2}=1$ and ${x}^{2}+z=4$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨2x,\,-z,\,-y⟩=\lambda ⟨0,\,1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩+\mu ⟨2x,\,0,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩ \\ y+{z}^{2}=1 \\ {x}^{2}+z=4\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing expressions?
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the maximum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-yz
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)=y+{z}^{2}=1,\,h(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+z=4.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=1 \\ h(x,y,z)=4\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨2x,\,-z,\,-y⟩ & =\lambda ⟨0,\,1,\,2z⟩+\mu ⟨2x,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
